question.problem:
Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(8,6)=0.8,\,F(8,2)=0.5,\,F(2,6)=0.4,\,F(2,2)=0.2.
$$

Find $P(2\le X\le 8,2\le Y\le 6).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233382/assets/1524afeeaea3cc0fd4ee51b9572222bdd846fba378e029e4fa20a272a4fe6353.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(8,6).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(8,2)$ and $(2,6).$

3\. Finally, we need to *add back* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(2,2).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le X\le 8,2\le Y\le 6) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(8,6)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 8,Y\le 6)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(8,2)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 8,Y\le 2)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(2,6)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 2,Y\le 6)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(2,2)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 2,Y\le 2)}} \\  & =F(8,6)-F(8,2)-F(2,6)+F(2,2) \\  & =0.8-0.5-0.4+0.2 \\  & =0.1.\end{aligned}
$$
